chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
One who is pleased that goodness should increase in his house, let him perform ablution (wudu) at the time his food is presented.
ai.seo_question: What is the benefit of performing ablution before eating according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) connects physical purity with domestic prosperity, suggesting that the ritual act of wudu upon the arrival of food serves as a spiritual catalyst for increased barakah in the household. This practice highlights the Shia emphasis on integrating ritual discipline into daily sustenance, transforming the mundane act of eating into a moment of spiritual mindfulness and divine grace.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘One who is gladdened that goodness should frequent his house, so let him perform ablution during the presentation of his meal’.
en.sarwar: 4. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from al-Nawfaliy from al-Sakuniy who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
If one likes to see blessings in his house to increase, he must take wudu for taking food.’”
